title: Platform Custodian Onramp — Pocket Deck (Draft)
content:
Slide 1 — Title: Platform Custodian Onramp — Pocket Deck (Draft)
Speaker note: One-pager / 5-min deck to help platform engineers (custodians) evaluate Redwood as an inference runtime. Goal: rapid pilot alignment, risk mitigation, and ops handoff.

Slide 2 — Persona & Why this matters
- Persona: Platform Custodian (infra/platform teams, internal shared services)
- Primary concerns: predictable capacity, auditability, network/VPC integration, key management, rollout control
- Sales angle: translation of our product differentiators into platform-grade constraints and migration checkpoints

Slide 3 — 3-minute risk-friendly pitch
- High-level: same API across hosted/dedicated/private -> reduces integration surface
- Reliability: canary + automatic fallbacks to compatible model variants
- Control: VPC peering, KMS integration, local audit logs
Speaker note: aim for confident 3-min opener for SEs

Slide 4 — Pilot 30/60/90 (practical checklist)
- 0-30: staging connectivity (VPC, firewall rules), auth proofs, 1 model smoke tests, baseline latency measurement (p50/p95)
- 30-60: throughput tuning (batching, cache rules), rollout of 10% traffic, cost estimation per 1k API calls
- 60-90: SLA targets agreed, production rollout plan, playbook for fallback and incident response

Slide 5 — Integration artifacts we need (minimal)
- Network: list of CIDR and NAT gateway rules to open
- Auth: token exchange/STS flows or mutual-TLS proof
- Logging: SIEM export path, retention window
- Key management: KMS/HSM integration details

Slide 6 — Quick operational play snippets (copyable)
- Canary plan: 5% traffic -> 20% -> 50% with 24h observation windows
- Fallback policy (example terms): fallback_to: [model-small, model-quant], max_latency_ms: 1200, degrade_after_errors: 3
Speaker note: this is intentionally non-prod syntax — for conversation only

Slide 7 — Cost/Performance heuristics for platform teams
- If p95 < 500ms and throughput < 200 req/s, start with x1 small dedicated pool
- For heavy embeddings pipelines: use caching + async batch workers (saves ~40–70% token cost)
- Quantization: test per-model accuracy delta on 5 eval prompts before production

Slide 8 — Common objections and knee-jerk responses
- "We need on-prem only" -> Redwood Private available with audit + air-gapped options
- "Cost unpredictable" -> Reserved Dedicated + Optimize tooling with batching recommendations
- "We can self-host cheaper" -> talk throughput engineering cost model and SRE burden

Slide 9 — Roleplay: 90s SE opener for custodian persona
- SE: "We focus on keeping core infra simple for app teams. Can you run a small canary in our staging VPC for 48h?"
- Platform: "We need KMS integration and SIEM hooks"
- SE: "We’ll provision a private deployment with customer-managed KMS and a 48h evidence package (latency/cost/traces)"

Slide 10 — Handoff checklist for post-sale engineering
- Shared runbook (owner, escalation path)
- Canaries + automatic rollback configured
- Cost alerts and token-level billing visibility enabled
- Security review sign-off (arch + sec)

Slide 11 — Open questions / TODOs (work-in-progress)
- Can we standardize a 5-step SIEM export template? @mruiz
- Validate KMS integration latency in eu-west-1 (perf team)
- Create a short demo harness that runs 1000 requests and outputs p50/p95/cost for the pilot (ops)

Slide 12 — Appendix: short checklist for SEs before demo
- Check customer IAM and firewall rules
- Prepare sample prompts and token budget
- Pre-wire fallback steps and rollback thresholds
- Slack shortcut: #pilot-handoff thread template

Notes / meta: This deck is intentionally compact — target size is 10–12 slides for a 5–8 minute walk-through with platform leads. Keep technical snippets conversational and avoid committing to exact SLA language here — move legal/contract details to dedicated doc. 

References: CONFL-PCON-001 for private deployment checklist; JIRA-1427 pilot task; slack thread #platform-seller-handoff (prep).
